howto.welcome_intro:
This comprehensive guide will help you create, manage and export custom vehicle skins for BeamNG.drive.

Whether you're a beginner or an experienced modder, this guide covers everything from basic skin creation to advanced custom vehicle integration.

howto_content.getting_started_content:
Welcome to BeamSkin Studio!

BeamSkin Studio turns your skin textures into a ready-to-play BeamNG.drive mod. You paint the texture, the program builds all the game files around it (materials, JBEAM, folders, ZIP).

What you need:

1. BeamNG.drive installed
2. An image editor that can save DDS files (Paint.NET, GIMP with a DDS plugin, Photoshop with a DDS plugin, or Substance Painter)
3. A UV template for your vehicle (you get this inside BeamSkin Studio, see below)

First-time setup (Settings tab):

• BeamNG.drive installation: the folder that contains the game (needed for "Get UV Map")
• BeamNG mods folder: where your finished mod is saved. Use Auto detect if you are not sure
• The setup wizard asks for both when you first start the program. You can change them any time in Settings

The 5-step workflow:

1. Car List tab: find your vehicle and click Get UV Map. Paint your skin on top of that template
2. Save your skin as a .dds file. The file name does not matter, BeamSkin Studio renames it for you
3. Project tab: type a Mod Name and Author, then add your vehicle from the sidebar
4. Select the vehicle, type a Skin Name, pick your DDS file and click Add skin
5. Choose where to save (sidebar, Output section) and click Generate Mod

Then start BeamNG.drive, spawn the vehicle, open the vehicle config and choose your skin in the Paint Design slot (see the Project Tab chapter).

Good habits:

• Click Save in the Project tab often. A saved project lets you update the mod later
• Keep your layered source file (PSD, XCF...) separate from the exported DDS
• Test with one simple skin before building a big mod

Common beginner mistakes:

• Saving the texture as PNG or JPG instead of DDS (normal skins need DDS)
• Painting without the UV template, so the design lands in the wrong place
• Using characters like \ / : * ? " < > | in the skin name
• Forgetting that the mod must be enabled in BeamNG and the game may need a restart
howto_content.skin_creation_content:
Creating a Skin

This chapter covers making the texture itself. Everything about adding it to a project is in the Project Tab chapter.

Step 1: Get the UV template

A UV map shows where each body part sits on the flat texture. Without it you are painting blind.

1. Open the Car List tab and find your vehicle
2. Click Get UV Map
3. If the vehicle has several UV files, tick the ones you want and save them
4. Open the template in your editor and keep it as the top layer (lower its opacity) while you paint underneath

Notes:

• Get UV Map reads the files from your BeamNG.drive install, so the installation path must be set in Settings
• For vehicles you added yourself (Add Vehicles tab), the button only appears if the mod came with UV images

Step 2: Paint the skin

• Match the template's width and height ratio (square or 2:1)
• Use a power-of-two size, for example 4096 x 4096. Go to 8192 only if you really need the detail, bigger files use more graphics memory and are slower to load
• Keep important details away from UV seams and edges
• Work in layers and keep a master file (.psd, .xcf, .kra)

Step 3: Export as DDS

• Format: DDS
• Compression: BC7 if your editor has it. If not, use BC3 (DXT5) for textures with transparency, or BC1 (DXT1) for opaque ones
• Turn mip maps on
• Hide or remove the UV template layer before exporting

File name:

You can name the file anything. BeamSkin Studio copies it into the mod and renames it to carid_skin_SkinName.dds automatically, and points the game files to it. The name that matters is the Skin Name you type in the Project tab.

Skin Name rules:

• Spaces are fine, the in-game name will be exactly what you type
• Do not use \ / : * ? " < > |
• Every skin on the same vehicle needs a different name

Before you export:

☐ Design lines up with the UV template
☐ No important detail on a seam
☐ Template layer hidden
☐ Saved as DDS
☐ Master file saved
howto_content.skin_color_content:
Colorable Skins

A colorable skin lets the player pick the paint colors in-game, using BeamNG's normal paint menu. Your artwork stays, and chosen areas change color.

How it works in BeamNG:

BeamNG vehicles have three paint colors: Paint 1, Paint 2 and Paint 3. A colorable skin uses two images to decide what shows where.

• Base Color Map: your artwork. Logos, decals, sponsor stickers, shading, anything that must always look the same
• Color Palette Map: tells the game which paint color goes where, using the red, green and blue channels

The Color Palette Map colors:

• Pure red (255, 0, 0) = Paint 1
• Pure green (0, 255, 0) = Paint 2
• Pure blue (0, 0, 255) = Paint 3

So you get at most three separate colorable areas. Use pure colors, not shades. Blending two of them gives a gradient between the two paint colors.

Making the two maps:

1. Open the UV template and paint your artwork. Leave the areas that should show the player's paint transparent
2. Create the palette map at the same size: fill each area with pure red, green or blue depending on which paint color it should use
3. Export both as PNG (not DDS). Keep the transparency

Adding it in the Project tab:

1. Select the vehicle and type the Skin Name
2. Turn on Colorable skin
3. Pick the Base Color Map and the Color Palette Map. Both are required
4. Click Add skin

If the vehicle has a variant body (for example a pickup box), you need a pair of maps for the normal body and a second pair for the variant body.

Tips:

• Test in-game, then change the paint colors in the game's paint menu to see each area react
• Keep fine detail in the Base Color Map. Keep the palette map flat and simple
• Colorable skins use PNG, normal skins use DDS

Image example:
{{img:colorpalettemap.png|250|Color Palette Map}}
{{img:Basecolormap.png|250|Base Color Map}}
howto_content.skin_reflective_content:
Reflective and Glowing Parts

Some parts of a skin can do more than just have a color: they can be retroreflective (like road signs and safety tape, which throw headlight beams straight back) or glow.

Both are done with Custom Layers in the Project tab. A custom layer is an extra material layer placed on top of your skin.

Limit:

BeamNG allows a maximum of 4 material layers per skin. The skin itself uses some of them, so you can usually add about two custom layers. When you reach the limit, the + Add Layer button tells you.

Retroreflective parts:

You need:

• A texture for the layer (its Base Color Map, a .dds). Use your skin texture or a rough/metallic map
• An Opacity Map (PNG): white = this area retroreflects, black = it does not. Light gray gives a weaker effect

Steps:

1. Make the Opacity Map at your UV size: fill it black, then paint white over the signs, tape or markings
2. Select the vehicle, fill in the skin as usual
3. Under Custom Layers, click + Add Layer
4. Set the layer's base color map and its Opacity Map
5. Set Retroreflectivity to 1 (0 = off)
6. Add the skin

Example (police livery): base skin, rough/metallic map, and retroreflective mask.
{{img:reflectivebase.png|250|Base skin}}
{{img:reflectivered.png|250|Roughness/Metallic map}}
{{img:poliskombi_retro_mask.data.png|250|Retroreflective mask}}

Layer settings:

• Metallic Factor, Roughness Factor, Clear Coat Factor, Clear Coat Roughness: how shiny the layer is (0 to 1)
• Normal Map, Opacity Map, and detail maps: optional extras
• Detail Scale: how often detail maps repeat. Higher = smaller pattern

Glowing parts:

1. Turn on Glowing Skin (in the skin or in a layer)
2. Select the Emissive Map (.dds). Bright areas glow, dark areas do not
3. Add the skin

Tips:

• Test at night with headlights on, retroreflection is easiest to see in the dark
• Keep the mask exact. Reflective areas that do not match your artwork look like floating patches
• Older projects that used the previous Retroreflective toggle are converted to a custom layer automatically when loaded
howto_content.project_content:
The Project Tab

The Project tab is where you build your mod. One project = one mod (one ZIP), with any number of vehicles, and any number of skins per vehicle.

The sidebar:

• Mod Name: becomes the ZIP / folder name. Spaces are turned into underscores automatically
• Author Name: written into the skin files, shown in BeamNG
• Add vehicle to project: search and click a vehicle to add it to the project
• Vehicles in project: your selected vehicles and their skins
• Output: where and how the mod is saved

Adding a vehicle:

1. Search for the vehicle in the sidebar list
2. Click its card. It moves into Vehicles in project
3. Each vehicle can only be added once. A vehicle can hold as many skins as you like
4. Some vehicles have a variant body (for example the Pickup box). Open the vehicle's group to add the variant. A variant needs one texture for the normal body and one for the variant body

Adding a skin:

1. Click the vehicle in your project so it is selected
2. Type a Skin Name (this is the name shown in-game)
3. Click Browse next to Skin File (DDS) and choose your texture. If you picked a variant body, also choose the variant texture
4. Optional: use the extra sections below
5. Click Add skin
6. Click a skin in the list to edit it, then Update skin. The remove button deletes it

If you turn on Colorable skin, you choose a Base Color Map and Color Palette Map (PNG) instead of a DDS. See the Colorable Skins chapter.

Optional extras (per skin):

Add Config:
• Also creates a vehicle config in the game's vehicle selector that uses your skin
• Needs a Config name, a Type, a .pc file (vehicle config exported from BeamNG) and a .jpg picture
• Edit Vehicle Info lets you change the info shown for the config. Empty fields keep the default

Edit material properties:
• Change Metallic, Roughness, Clear Coat and similar values of the paint (0 to 1, or empty)
• Presets: save your favorite settings and load them later

Custom Layers and Glowing:
• Extra material layers, retroreflective parts and glowing. See the Reflective Skins chapter

Use Secondary UV:
• Try this if your skin looks wrong or misplaced on the vehicle

Saving the project:

• Save writes a project file (.json). Next saves overwrite the same file
• Save as... writes a new file
• Load opens the project browser with your recent projects. You can also add old files with Add Existing Save
• Clear removes all vehicles and skins and also empties Mod Name and Author. It asks first and cannot be undone
• The program warns about unsaved changes before you load or clear
• If a texture file was moved or deleted, Generate stops and lists the missing files. Fix them by selecting the skin again

Output:

• ZIP: one .zip file. Best for sharing
• Unpacked: a normal folder. Best for quick testing and editing
• Mods Folder: saves into the mods folder from Settings. Unpacked mods go in a subfolder called unpacked inside it
• Custom Location: any folder you choose with Browse

Generating:

1. Make sure Mod Name and Author are filled, and every vehicle has at least one skin
2. Click Generate Mod
3. If a mod with the same name already exists in the output folder, you are asked if you want to overwrite it
4. A progress bar shows the steps. A success message appears when it is done

Testing in BeamNG.drive:

1. Start the game (restart it if it was running while you generated the mod)
2. Make sure the mod is enabled in the Mod Manager
3. Spawn the vehicle
4. Open the vehicle configuration, go to Parts and find the Paint Design slot, then choose your skin by its Skin Name
5. If you added a Config, it also appears as its own configuration in the vehicle selector

Skin not showing?
• Check the mod is enabled and restart BeamNG
• Check you picked the right vehicle
• Check Troubleshooting chapter
howto_content.car_list_content:
The Car List Tab

The Car List shows every vehicle BeamSkin Studio knows, including the ones you added yourself. Use it to find a vehicle, copy its ID and get its UV template.

Finding a vehicle:

• Type in the search box. It searches the name and the ID as you type
• Switch between Classic (compact list) and Modern (large cards) with the view button
• Hover over a vehicle for half a second to see its preview picture

Each vehicle card shows:

• The vehicle name (how it appears in-game)
• The car ID (the internal name, usually lowercase, sometimes with underscores)
• Get UV Map
• Copy ID

Get UV Map:

1. Click Get UV Map on the vehicle
2. If there is more than one UV file, choose which ones to save
3. Choose where to save them
4. Open the file in your image editor and use it as a guide layer

Requirements:
• Your BeamNG.drive installation folder must be set in Settings
• For vehicles you added yourself, the button only shows if the mod included UV images

Car ID:

The car ID is the vehicle's internal name, for example etk800 or pickup. BeamSkin Studio uses it for you when it builds the mod, so you normally do not need to type it anywhere. It matters when you add custom vehicles (see Add Vehicle), and Copy ID is handy for notes, forum posts or bug reports.

Vehicle name vs car ID:

• Name: "Gavril D-Series". Can contain spaces
• ID: "pickup". No spaces

Missing preview picture:

Some vehicles show a placeholder image. It does not affect anything.
howto_content.uv_exporter_content:
The UV Exporter Tab

The UV Exporter makes a UV template PNG straight from a vehicle's 3D model (.dae), so you can paint on top of it. It works for BeamNG vehicles and for vehicles you added from mods.

Opening a model:

• From the Car List: click UV Template on a vehicle
• Or drop any .dae file on the drop zone, or click it to browse

Where the model comes from:

• Vehicles from BeamNG.drive are read from your installation. The installation path must be set in Settings
• Vehicles you added in the Add Vehicles tab are looked up in the mod they came from. BeamSkin Studio remembers that location (folder or ZIP) automatically when you add the vehicle
• If a vehicle has more than one .dae file, pick one from the list. The largest (usually the main body) is loaded first

If the model is not found:

1. Click Locate mod
2. Choose Folder, ZIP or .dae file and select where the mod is
3. BeamSkin Studio checks that a model is there, remembers the location and loads it

You only need to do this once per vehicle. If you move or delete the mod, the tab tells you the saved location is missing, and you can locate it again.

Step 1: Groups to include

Every mesh group (material) of the model is listed with its triangle count. Only checked groups are drawn.

• All / None: check or uncheck everything
• Only shown: check what matches the current search and uncheck the rest
• Auto: checks the parts that look paintable and unchecks mechanical parts, overlay materials and broken UVs. Hover an unchecked item to see why
• Search: filters the list. A warning appears if checked groups are hidden by the search

Some models have several UV channels. If so, a UV channel selector appears.

Step 2: Template options

• Width and Height: 512 to 16384 px. 4096 is the default. 16K is very large and can take a long time
• Line width and Line color
• Color-code by material/group: gives each group its own color
• Checker background: a scale reference
• Island outlines only: draws only the outer edge of each UV island
• Hide quad diagonals: gives a clean quad grid
• Fill islands with color: fills islands with a translucent color. Set the color and opacity

The preview is a low-resolution proxy. The export is rendered at the full size you chose.

Step 3: Export

1. Click Export UV Template PNG
2. Choose where to save it
3. Open the PNG in your image editor and use it as a guide layer

Saving your selection:

Save selection for this file remembers the checked groups, UV channel and options for that model, and applies them next time (turn off Auto-apply saved selection on load to disable this). Clear removes it. Your selection is also saved automatically after a successful export.

Tips:

• Start with Auto, then fix the few groups it got wrong
• Use a transparent PNG as the top layer and lower its opacity while painting
• Export at the same size as your skin texture
howto_content.beamng_parts_content:
Loading BeamNG Parts

The 3D preview can show exactly the parts of the vehicle you spawned in BeamNG (wheels, body variant, options). For that it needs a parts export from the BeamSkin Studio exporter mod, a small UI app that runs inside BeamNG.

Getting the mod:

• Click Load BeamNG parts… in the preview. If the mod is not installed, BeamSkin Studio tells you and offers Install to BeamNG
• Install copies the mod to your BeamNG mods/unpacked folder. It works the same in the .exe version, the mod is included with the app
• Exporter mod setup… in the preview installs, updates or shows the mod at any time
• If the mod folder cannot be found, click Locate mod folder… or copy beamskin_studio_exporter_mod into mods/unpacked yourself

Creating an export:

1. Start BeamNG.drive. Restart it if it was already open when you installed the mod
2. Spawn the vehicle with the parts you want to preview
3. Open the UI apps menu, Vehicle Info category, and add BeamSkin Studio - Vehicle Parts Exporter
4. Pick a preset name and press Export current vehicle parts
5. The app confirms the file it wrote

Loading it:

1. In the preview, click Load BeamNG parts…
2. Pick the .json from settings/beamskin_studio/<vehicle id>
3. The matching parts are ticked and placed like in the game

Tips:

• Export again after changing parts in the game
• The export must be for the same vehicle as the preview
• Auto in the parts list drops the loaded BeamNG parts
howto_content.add_vehicle_content:
The Add Vehicles Tab

Use this tab to add vehicles that are not in the list yet: modded vehicles or newly released ones. After adding, the vehicle shows up in the Car List and in the Project sidebar.

The tab has two sub-tabs:

• Vehicles: for vehicles with the normal skin setup (one texture)
• Variants: for body shapes that need two textures (2 DDS / 4 PNGs), for example the box body of the Pickup

What the program needs from a mod:

• A materials .json file for the skins (for example skin.materials.json)
• A .jbeam file that defines the skin (for example main.jbeam)
• Optional: a preview image and UV map images

You do not have to find these yourself. Use Auto-Import.

Auto-Import (recommended):

1. Open the Add Vehicles tab
2. Click Browse Folder (an extracted mod) or Browse ZIP (one or more mod .zip files)
3. Wait for the scan. Each ZIP shows a status: queued, scanning, done, empty or failed
4. Look at the results list. Each row shows the car ID it found, an editable display name, and chips for JSON, JBEAM and IMG
5. Only rows that have both JSON and JBEAM are ticked and can be imported. A warning icon explains what is missing
6. Edit the display name if you want, then click Add Checked
7. A message tells you how many were imported

How the scanner works:

• It looks for a vehicles folder in the mod and checks each folder inside it
• Folders called common or containing traffic are skipped on purpose
• The folder name is the car ID
• If the car ID already exists in your list, the scanner treats it as a possible variant instead
• Vehicles you already added are hidden, so scanning the same mod twice is safe

Where is the mod?

• Downloaded mods are in your BeamNG mods folder as .zip files. You can point Auto-Import at the ZIP directly
• Stock game vehicles are already in the list

Manual Entry (if Auto-Import cannot find the files):

1. Open Manual Entry
2. Vehicle ID: the exact name of the vehicle's folder inside the mod's vehicles folder, same capitalization. Example: vehicles/custom_rally_car/ gives custom_rally_car
3. Display Name: any name you like
4. materials.json: browse to the skin materials file
5. .jbeam file: browse to the skin jbeam file
6. Optional preview image (.jpg) and UV map
7. Click Add Vehicle

Variants:

On the Variants tab, enter the variant suffix (for example box), the variant materials .json and .jbeam. The program creates the template so the Project tab can offer that body. Auto-Import also finds variants.

Checking the result:

1. The vehicle shows up in the Car List
2. In the Project tab, add it and make a simple test skin (one flat color)
3. Generate, then check the skin in BeamNG's Paint Design slot

Removing a vehicle:

Added vehicles are listed at the bottom with a Delete button. Deleting asks for confirmation.

Problems:

"Nothing found" or "empty":
→ The mod may not have a vehicles folder at the top level. Try the extracted folder instead of the ZIP
→ The mod may have no skin files (not every vehicle mod supports skins)

"Not ready to import":
→ Hover the warning icon, it says if the JSON or JBEAM is missing. Use Manual Entry and choose the files yourself

"The skin does not show in the game":
→ The Vehicle ID must match the vehicle folder name exactly
→ The mod containing the vehicle must also be installed and enabled in BeamNG

Note: support for modded vehicles is still limited. Some mods use unusual file setups and may not work.
howto_content.troubleshooting_content:
Troubleshooting

Find your problem and follow the checks in order.

The skin does not appear in BeamNG:

1. Is the mod in your mods folder (or unpacked folder) and enabled in the Mod Manager?
2. Restart BeamNG completely
3. Spawn the vehicle, open its configuration, go to Parts and look at the Paint Design slot. Skins are chosen there
4. Did you pick the correct vehicle in the Project tab?
5. Was the mod generated into the folder BeamNG actually uses? Check the mods folder path in Settings
6. Is another mod with the same vehicle skin name conflicting? Try a new Mod Name

Generate Mod gives an error or does nothing:

• "Please enter a ZIP name" or author: fill in Mod Name and Author
• "Please add at least one vehicle" or "add a skin": every vehicle needs at least one skin
• "Missing files": a texture was moved or deleted. Select it again
• "Two skins produce the same folder name": give each skin on a vehicle a different name
• "Mods folder does not exist": set it in Settings, or switch to Custom Location
• Skin name error: remove \ / : * ? " < > | from the skin name
• "File not found: template": the vehicle template is missing. Re-add the vehicle in Add Vehicles
• Turn on Debug mode in Settings and read the console for the real error

A mod with this name already exists:

You are asked if you want to overwrite it. Choose yes to replace it, or cancel and change the Mod Name. If the overwrite fails, BeamNG may have the file open: close BeamNG and try again.

Texture problems (DDS):

• Skin looks wrong or in the wrong place: use the UV template, or try Use Secondary UV
• Black or white texture: check the file was exported correctly and has the expected size, try BC7 or BC3
• Looks corrupted: re-export from your source file, generate mip maps, try another compression
• Texture is blurry up close: use a higher resolution (4096 or 8192)
• Game stutters or loads slowly: texture too big, reduce size

Colorable skin problems:

• Only one color shows: check the palette map uses pure red, green and blue
• Wrong areas change color: red = Paint 1, green = Paint 2, blue = Paint 3
• Artwork is missing: check the Base Color Map was selected and is PNG

Custom layers:

• "Maximum number of layers": BeamNG allows 4 layers in total per skin. Remove a layer
• "Layer is missing its file": every layer needs its base color map, and glowing layers need an emissive map

Project problems:

• Cannot load a project: it must be a project .json file made by BeamSkin Studio
• Project missing in the browser: use Add Existing Save to add the file again
• Cannot save: check that the folder is writable and has free space

Settings and paths:

• Mods folder not found: set it in Settings or in the setup wizard (Auto detect). It is usually in AppData\Local\BeamNG.drive, in the folder of your game version, under mods
• Get UV Map says path not configured: set the BeamNG.drive installation folder in Settings
• Preview slow for huge textures: turn off Texture Previews in Settings

The program:

• Crashes or errors: enable Debug mode and Log to File in Settings (log is data/app_log.txt)
• Online tab unavailable: the server may be down. All other features still work offline

Getting help:

Include what you did, what happened, your debug log, your operating system and your BeamNG version. Ask in the BeamNG modding community or report the problem through the program's online Report tab.
howto_content.advanced_content:
Advanced Topics

Multiple vehicles in one mod:

Add several vehicles to one project and give each its skins. Everything is exported into one ZIP. This is great for livery packs.

Variants and body types:

Some vehicles have extra bodies with their own texture (variant bodies). In a project they appear as separate entries and need their own texture.

Material properties:

Edit material properties changes how the paint reacts to light.
• Metallic: 0 = plastic or paint, 1 = metal
• Roughness: 0 = mirror, 1 = rough
• Clear Coat and Clear Coat Roughness: the glossy lacquer on top
Leave a value empty to keep the vehicle's default. Save presets to reuse the same finish.

Custom layers:

Use layers when part of the skin needs its own material (chrome, matte, carbon, retroreflective, glowing). Each layer has its own base color map, opacity map, normal map, factors and detail maps. A skin can have at most 4 material layers in total, including the ones the vehicle already uses.

Vehicle configs:

Add Config makes a ready-to-select vehicle setup in the game's vehicle selector. Export a .pc file from BeamNG with the parts you want, add a .jpg picture, and BeamSkin Studio links the config to your skin automatically.

Updating a mod:

1. Load your saved project
2. Change or add skins
3. Save, then Generate Mod with the same name and confirm the overwrite
4. Restart BeamNG

Data and backups:

Your added vehicles, projects and settings are stored in the BeamSkin Studio data folder (see Settings). You can move it to another drive there, and the program migrates old data automatically. Back this folder up.

Texture quality:

• Use the lowest resolution that still looks good for the vehicle size
• Do not scale a small texture up
• Check skins in daylight, at night, and in rain
• Check text and numbers are readable
howto_content.faq_content:
Frequently Asked Questions

Skins and textures:

Q: What file type do I need?
A: DDS for normal skins. PNG for colorable skins (Base Color Map and Color Palette Map).

Q: Does my DDS file need a special name?
A: No. BeamSkin Studio renames it for you. Only the Skin Name you type in the Project tab matters.

Q: Can I use spaces in the Skin Name?
A: Yes. Just avoid \ / : * ? " < > |

Q: What resolution should I use?
A: Match the UV template ratio and use a power of two, for example 4096 x 4096 (or 4096 x 2048 for 2:1). Go higher only if needed.

Q: How do I get the UV map?
A: Car List tab, Get UV Map. Set your BeamNG.drive install folder in Settings first.

Q: Can I use the same texture on a different vehicle?
A: No. Every vehicle has its own UV layout.

Q: How many colors can a colorable skin have?
A: Three: red, green and blue in the palette map are Paint 1, 2 and 3.

Using the program:

Q: Can I add several skins to one vehicle?
A: Yes, as many as you like, if each has a different name.

Q: Can one mod contain several vehicles?
A: Yes. That is the main purpose of projects.

Q: Can I add the same vehicle twice?
A: No. Add it once and give it several skins.

Q: What is the difference between ZIP and Unpacked?
A: ZIP is one file for sharing. Unpacked is a plain folder (saved in a folder called unpacked inside your mods folder) which is easier for testing and editing.

Q: How do I update a mod?
A: Load your project, change it, generate with the same Mod Name and confirm the overwrite.

Q: What happens to my project when I click Clear?
A: Everything is removed, including Mod Name and Author. Save first if you want to keep it.

Q: Where are my project files?
A: Wherever you saved them (.json). The Load button shows your recent projects.

In BeamNG.drive:

Q: Where do I choose my skin in the game?
A: Open the vehicle configuration, go to Parts, and find the Paint Design slot. If you added a Config, you also find it in the vehicle selector.

Q: Do I have to enable the mod?
A: Yes, check it is enabled in the Mod Manager and restart the game if the skin does not show.

Q: Why can't I see my skin?
A: Check the mod is enabled, restart BeamNG, and check the Troubleshooting chapter.

Q: Will other players see my skin in multiplayer?
A: Only if the server also provides the mod. A mod that is only in your own mods folder is only visible to you.

Vehicles:

Q: What is a car ID?
A: The vehicle's internal name, such as etk800. Find it in the Car List.

Q: Is it case-sensitive?
A: Treat it as case-sensitive. Auto-Import fills it in for you.

Q: Can I add mod vehicles?
A: Yes, in the Add Vehicles tab. Use Auto-Import first. Support for modded vehicles is still limited.
